# APT Versions

This page is for **operators** who run the `plugin-apt-versions` plugin with the CCF Agent, and for **developers** who write policies for it. It documents [v0.7.2](https://github.com/compliance-framework/plugin-apt-versions/releases/tag/v0.7.2) and is generated from the plugin's [README at v0.7.2](https://github.com/compliance-framework/plugin-apt-versions/blob/v0.7.2/README.md).

## How it works

### Usage

You can use this plugin by passing it to the compliance agent

```shell
agent --plugin=[PATH_TO_YOUR_BINARY]
```

## Requirements

### Prerequisites

* GoReleaser https://goreleaser.com/install/

## Policy input

One run lists the packages installed on the host with `dpkg-query` and evaluates every policy package against them. A policy receives the result as `input`: one key per installed package, named as dpkg names it, with the package's version as a string. The versions are normalised to `major.minor.patch` so that a policy can compare them: the epoch (the part before a `:`) is dropped, everything from the first `-`, `+` or `~` is cut, the text after the digits in each part is cut, leading zeros are removed, and the result is padded with `0` to three parts or cut to three. So `1:9.6p1-3ubuntu13.5` becomes `9.6.0`, and `3.0.13-0ubuntu3.4` becomes `3.0.13`. The original version string is not in the document. The keys depend on the host, so the table lists the shape of a key. A package that is not installed is missing from the document, so test for it, or give it a default. A package name with a dot or a dash is read with brackets: `input["libssl3"]`. Your own policy data from the agent configuration is in `data.<key>`, not in `input`.

| Field | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `<package name>` | string | The normalised version of the installed package, such as `3.0.13`. One key for each package `dpkg-query` lists. |

An example input:

```json
{
  "bash": "5.2.21",
  "libssl3": "3.0.13",
  "openssh-server": "9.6.0",
  "openssl": "3.0.13",
  "sudo": "1.9.15"
}
```

## Subject templates

The subject templates this plugin registers. Each example is built from sample data.

### APT Installed Package

Registered when the agent calls `Init`, with one subject per package and host. Title: `APT Package Component: '{{.package_name}}' on host: '{{.hostname}}'`. The `package_name` label is not set by the plugin's evidence at this release: the plugin labels every evidence with `type` (`apt`) and `hostname` only, so an evidence links to a subject of this template only when a policy sets a `package_name` label on it. The evidence's own subject is the machine instance, `machine-instance/<hostname>`.

| Identity key | Description |
|---|---|
| `hostname` | The `HOSTNAME` environment variable of the agent's process. It is empty when the variable isn't exported. |
| `package_name` | The name of the installed APT package, as dpkg names it. |
| `_plugin` | The name the plugin has in the agent configuration, set by the agent (`apt_versions` in the sample configuration). |

Example:

```json
{
  "name": "APT Installed Package",
  "type": "component",
  "title": "APT Package Component: 'openssl' on host: 'web-01'",
  "description": "Installed APT package 'openssl' on host: 'web-01'",
  "purpose": "Track installed APT package and its version",
  "identityLabels": {
    "hostname": "web-01",
    "package_name": "openssl",
    "_plugin": "apt_versions"
  }
}
```
